solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dish of peeled eggs in spinach regularly repulsed

indicators.note: repulsed means pushed back, so the assembled letters are read backwards
in places the trimmed eggs inside the picked letters of spinach
regularly picks every other letter of spinach, starting with the first
peeled strips the outer letters, like a shell, from eggs

explanation.surface: A recipe for a dish of shelled eggs set in spinach that diners turned away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peeled eggs' looks like part of the dish, but 'peeled' strips the shell letters; 'repulsed' reverses the whole assembly, SIGGAH.
explanation.definitionFit: Haggis is the Scottish national dish of offal and oats cooked in a casing.

clue.text: One of fifty that might be baked

definitions.meaning: One of the fifty United States
baked ... is a dessert of ice cream in browned meringue

explanation.surface: A riddle about something among fifty that could go in the oven.
explanation.definitionFit: Alaska is a US state, and baked Alaska is a well-known pudding.

clue.text: Bird's cunning circling large cat in ascent

indicators.note: circling means going round, so guile wraps around the letter for large

parts.note: cunning as a noun means guile
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

indicators.note: in a down clue, an ascent reads the word for cat from bottom to top

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A bird's crafty trick of circling a big cat as it climbs.
explanation.definitionFit: The guillemot is a black-and-white seabird of the auk family that nests on cliffs.

clue.text: Gets bigger and bigger drinks

definitions.meaning: a situation that ... grows rapidly, like a rolling snowball
a snowball is a cocktail of advocaat and lemonade

explanation.surface: Someone who grows larger with every round they order.
explanation.definitionFit: Snowballing means growing ever faster; snowballs are also advocaat cocktails.

clue.text: Aristocratic lady boozers collecting jokes

indicators.note: collecting means gathering in, so the pubs take the jokes inside them

parts.note: boozer is British slang for a pub, so boozers are bars
a joke can be called a 'one', as in 'that's a good one'

explanation.surface: A titled woman doing the rounds of the pubs gathering funny stories.
explanation.definitionFit: A baroness is a female peer, holding the lowest rank of the British peerage.

clue.text: Funds covering half of this spread

indicators.note: in a down clue, covering puts the money word on top of what follows

parts.note: bread is slang for money

indicators.note: half of takes the first two of the four letters of this

explanation.surface: Money that pays for half of this sandwich spread.
explanation.definitionFit: Breadth is the width or extent of something, the amount it spreads across.

clue.text: Bit in Delhi game originally played early evening

parts.note: RU is rugby union

indicators.note: originally takes the opening letter of each of the three words that follow

explanation.surface: A snippet of a match in Delhi that kicked off in the early evening.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'bit' is old slang for a coin, so 'Bit in Delhi' is a coin used there.
explanation.definitionFit: The rupee is the currency unit of India, whose capital is Delhi.

clue.text: Migrant relative overwhelmed by positive gesture

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means swallowed up, so the relative goes inside the gesture

parts.note: a nod is a gesture of agreement
ma, short for mother, is a relative

explanation.surface: A relative who has migrated is moved by a friendly signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomad wanders from place to place with no fixed home, migrating constantly.

clue.text: Periodically 34 emus line up

indicators.note: up here means in disorder or astir, so the letters of emus and line are jumbled

explanation.surface: Every so often thirty-four emus form a queue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Periodically' is not an alternate-letter signal: it points to the periodic table, where element 34 sits.
explanation.definitionFit: Selenium has atomic number 34, its place in the periodic table of elements.

clue.text: Cold author and swimmer sharing small undergarment

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
Kingsley or Martin Amis, British novelists

indicators.note: sharing means the author and the fish use one letter between them, so the shared letter for small appears once

parts.note: a sole is a flatfish

explanation.surface: A chilly writer and a swimmer squeezing into one small piece of underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: AMIS ends and SOLE starts with S; 'sharing small' overlaps them on that one S to give AMISOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A camisole is a light sleeveless top worn as underwear by women.

clue.text: Spot of fortune inspiring politician

indicators.note: inspiring, read as breathing in, has the fortune take the politician inside

parts.note: a pile is a large sum of money, a fortune
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A spot of luck that encourages someone in politics.
explanation.definitionFit: A pimple is a small inflamed spot on the skin.

clue.text: Island dog picked up satellite that fell to earth

indicators.note: picked up means heard, as by a microphone, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: Skye is a Scottish island and a lab is a Labrador dog

explanation.surface: A dog on a Scottish island hears a satellite crash.
explanation.walkthrough: Skye is an island of the Scottish Inner Hebrides.
explanation.definitionFit: Skylab was the US space station that came down over Australia in 1979.

clue.text: Not looking forward to daughter attending recital

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees
a reading is a recital of a text

explanation.surface: A parent nervous about going to their daughter's recital.
explanation.definitionFit: To be dreading something is to anticipate it with fear.

clue.text: Remains of Hindu retreat after stuff stolen

indicators.note: stolen means taken away, so the word for stuff is removed

parts.note: an ashram is a Hindu hermitage or retreat
to ram means to stuff or cram

explanation.surface: What is left of a Hindu retreat after a burglary.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash is the powdery residue left after burning, as in cremated remains.

clue.text: Lovers of altitude climb huge hill mostly drunk

indicators.note: drunk means unsteady and jumbled, so these letters are mixed up
mostly means most of the word, losing its final letter

explanation.surface: Mountaineers scaling a big hill while drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: The mile-high club is the jokey name for people who have had sex aboard an aircraft in flight.

clue.text: Fly solo in gale too high

indicators.note: high means intoxicated, so the letters reel into a new order

explanation.surface: A pilot flying alone at altitude in a strong wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word but is part of the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To go it alone is to act independently, without help, as a solo flyer does.

clue.text: 1,200 inches of creepy-crawly?

parts.note: 1,200 inches is a hundred feet, and this creature's name means a hundred feet

explanation.surface: A tape-measure reading for the length of some bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 1,200 inches is 100 feet; the creature's Latin-based name means 'hundred feet', so the clue counts its feet, not its length.
explanation.definitionFit: A centipede is a many-legged arthropod whose name means hundred-footed.

clue.text: Poet struggling to accept turn as novelist

indicators.note: to accept means to take in, so the jumbled poet holds the turn inside
struggling means in disarray, so the letters of poet are rearranged

parts.note: a roll is a turn or rotation

explanation.surface: A poet having trouble coming to terms with becoming a novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' turns Poet into TOPE; 'to accept' puts ROLL inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Trollope was the Victorian author of the Barsetshire novels.

clue.text: Outcry in support of extremely tame channel

parts.note: pro means in favour of

indicators.note: extremely takes the end letters of tame

parts.note: a TV or radio station is a channel

explanation.surface: An uproar backing a very dull television channel.
explanation.definitionFit: A protestation is a strong objection or declaration, an outcry against something.

clue.text: 25 in wood reported

indicators.note: reported means spoken of, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: yew is a wood, from the yew tree

explanation.surface: Something numbered 25 is said to be in the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 refers to the answer at 25-across, ANIMAL, of which this is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewe, a female sheep, is an example of the cross-referenced animal.

clue.text: One of twelve staff drenched in beer

indicators.note: drenched in means soaked inside, so the staff sits within the beer

parts.note: ale is beer
a post is a staff or pole

explanation.surface: A member of a twelve-strong workforce soaked in beer.
explanation.definitionFit: The twelve apostles were the disciples chosen by Jesus to spread his teaching.

clue.text: Clumsy cowboy finally replaced by European

indicators.note: finally replaced by swaps the final letter of the cowboy for the European letter

parts.note: a gaucho is a South American cowboy

explanation.surface: An awkward cowboy is at last superseded by a European.
explanation.definitionFit: Gauche means socially awkward or tactless, a borrowing from French 'left'.

clue.text: Fellow wounded officer gets a dance

parts.note: lame means injured in the leg
NCO is a non-commissioned officer

explanation.surface: A man's injured officer gets up to dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Flamenco is the passionate Andalusian Spanish dance style.

clue.text: Organisation that assesses unoccupied Iraq?

parts.note: Iraq emptied of its middle leaves IQ, which this society tests

explanation.surface: A political question about a body inspecting a post-occupation Iraq.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unoccupied' means emptied: Iraq without its inner letters is IQ.
explanation.definitionFit: Mensa is the society for people scoring highly on intelligence tests.

clue.text: Compound somewhat disconcerting after revolution

indicators.note: after revolution means turned around, so the letters run backwards
somewhat means part of, so a run of letters is taken from inside disconcerting

explanation.surface: A chemical compound that is a bit unsettling after an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitre is potassium nitrate, a chemical compound used in gunpowder.

clue.text: Show's drummer echoed beat in centre of stage

indicators.note: echoed means sent back, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or beat

indicators.note: centre of takes the middle letter of stage

explanation.surface: A drummer in a show repeating a beat in the middle of the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Animal is the wild drummer of the Muppet Show band.

clue.text: It might be Scotch that's covering the engine

definitions.meaning: a Scotch ... is a hot chilli pepper, and a ... is also a Scottish cap
the hinged hood over a car's engine

explanation.surface: Something Scottish that sits over a motor.
explanation.walkthrough: The bonnet is the British name for a car's hood.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotch bonnet is a variety of chilli; the bonnet is also a car's engine cover.

clue.text: Coin with old VP next to Trump's head

indicators.note: head means the first letter of the word Trump

parts.note: Mike Pence was the US Vice President

explanation.surface: A coin featuring a former vice president beside Trump's head.
explanation.walkthrough: Twopence is a British coin, two pennies.
explanation.definitionFit: Twopence is a British coin worth two pennies.

clue.text: Winds stopping fish going west? It's baffling

indicators.note: stopping means plugging, so the winds fill the middle of the reversed fish
going west in an across clue means read right to left

parts.note: an eel is a fish
gales are strong winds

explanation.surface: Strong winds stopping fish swimming westward, a puzzling sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Legalese is the jargon of lawyers, notoriously hard for laypeople to follow.

clue.text: The Spanish fair being a prime example

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
even means fair or balanced

explanation.surface: A fair in Spain is held up as a fine case.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleven is a prime number, divisible only by one and itself.
